//: Keyboard-mode shortcuts. Press Esc anywhere in SLICC to enter keyboard mode;
the keys then work on their own, with no modifier. Edit this file and reload
the tab to change them — it is read once at startup.
This file holds OVERRIDES only, and ships empty: the shipped keymap lives in
SLICC itself, so whatever you do not mention here follows it, including any
keys a later version adds. Press ? in keyboard mode to see what is bound.
Each entry is "key": "command". A key is a single character ("x") or a named
key ("Enter", "Tab", "Backspace", "Delete", "Home", "End", "ArrowLeft",
"ArrowRight", "ArrowUp", "ArrowDown"). Several keys may share one command.
A command with no key left is simply unreachable from the keyboard.
To REMOVE a binding, set it to null. Deleting a line does NOT remove the key —
it restores whatever SLICC ships for it.
Commands: composer, nextAgent, prevAgent, newConversation,
newConversationErase, newCone, dropCone, sessions, stop, approvals, attach,
copyReply, copyChat, leftRail, rightRail, files, tabs, terminal, memory,
monitor, sprinkles, cycleSprinkles, zoom, model, accounts, help.
Some commands own a list, and a digit pressed straight after them picks from
it instead of from the tab strip: files, memory, sessions and sprinkles. So
f 3 is the third file and r 9 is the oldest archived chat — 9 is always the
last one, exactly as it is for agents.
Esc and the digits 1-9 are reserved: Esc is the mode itself, and the digits
address the tab strip by position (9 is always the last agent).
Example — the SLICC 6.110 keyboard, if you had it in your fingers:
"bindings": {
"d": "nextAgent", "c": "composer", "n": "newConversation",
"b": "leftRail", "x": "rightRail", "f": "files", "t": "tabs",
"e": "terminal", "m": "memory", "s": "cycleSprinkles",
"l": "model", "a": "accounts", "h": "help", "/": "help"
This file is yours — SLICC only writes it when it is missing.
